key_insight: A total-pressure formulation enables locking-free poroelastic optimal control with first-order error estimates uniform as the Lamé parameter increases.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports source-control design in nearly incompressible porous materials while tracking displacement and fluid pressure under box constraints.
method: Use a mechanical Schur complement to establish zero-storage well-posedness for each fixed finite Lamé parameter.
Discretize states and adjoints with conforming finite elements and dG(0) time stepping.
Represent bounded source controls with piecewise constant functions.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments confirm predicted convergence rates, examine Lamé- and storage-coefficient dependence, and demonstrate localized pressure control with active bounds.
watch_item: The uniform first-order error estimates require stated regularity assumptions and a positive storage lower bound; they do not establish zero-storage convergence.
paper_title: Locking-free numerical methods for poroelasticity optimal control problems with minimal regularities
